evidence.note: Built an independent PyTorch reference TriMul (test_correct.py) from the spec einsum and compared the kernel against it, rather than asserting correctness from running without error.

Maintained test_more.py, a parametrized sweep over normal/cauchy distributions and mask/nomask states across multiple shapes, reporting per-shape max_abs and fail counts; re-ran it as a regression gate after changes.
Reasoned explicitly about the stated tolerance (allclose |a-b|<=atol+rtol|b|, rtol=atol=2e-2) and that a single failing element fails the grader — using the correct tolerance semantics.
Treated Cauchy mismatches as blocking failures, localized the cause to bf16 precision casts, and reverted those optimizations to preserve correctness — separating 'math right' from 'tolerance met'.

Flagged Cauchy heavy tails as the numerically hardest corner (fp32 accumulation/precision), showing deliberate awareness of the stress case, though N=2048+Cauchy correctness was not clearly exercised.

reasoning: The agent constructed a trustworthy independent PyTorch oracle and ran a repeated parametrized sweep across shapes, both mask states, and both distributions at the stated 2e-2 tolerance, treating any mismatch (notably Cauchy failures from bf16 casts) as blocking and localizing the cause — squarely the level-8 behavior. It stops short of level 10 because the reference was never independently cross-verified against the einsum a second way, the full batch×N×dim grid (dim=768, largest-N Cauchy) was not exhaustively stressed, though it showed clear awareness of Cauchy as the hard corner.
